{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABXrc8ag", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6PzhBPqVc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 78, "title": "Experiment with YXZ Euler rotation order for MMD rigid-body offsets", "body": "## Problem

The current [`MMDPhysics.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts#L773-L783) builds rotation transforms from `new Euler()` / `Euler.set(x, y, z)`, which defaults to **XYZ** in Three.js. Both rigid-body offsets ([`RigidBody._init()`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts#L1256-L1267)) and joint frames ([`Constraint._init()`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts#L1471-L1488)) currently call the same `ResourceManager.setBasisFromArray3()` helper.

Other MMD implementations suggest a different rigid-body rotation convention:

- [Saba, PMD/PMX rigid-body creation](https://github.com/benikabocha/saba/blob/master/src/Saba/Model/MMD/MMDPhysics.cpp) constructs the original-coordinate rotation matrix as `Ry * Rx * Rz` (YXZ matrix product).
- [babylon-mmd Bullet rigid-body construction](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/mmdBulletPhysics.ts) uses `Quaternion.FromEulerAnglesToRef(x, y, z)`, corresponding to the same YXZ product under Babylon's convention.
- [mmd-parser coordinate conversion](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-parser/blob/master/src/DataCreationHelper.ts#L22-L27) negates Euler X/Y for the left-to-right-handed conversion; this does **not** itself change the Euler composition order. [`MMDLoader`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/loaders/MMDLoader.ts#L180-L186) parses with right-handed conversion enabled.

Thus our **rigid-body** XYZ composition may differ for combined-axis rotations. This is a static-analysis hypothesis; it is **not** yet proof of exact MikuMikuDance parity, a demonstrated user-visible regression, or the cause of intermittent violent physics oscillations.

There is a second implementation path: [`WorkerPhysicsAdapter.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/WorkerPhysicsAdapter.ts#L230-L240) independently builds `this.offsets` with `new Euler(...body.rotation)` (also XYZ). Changing only the Bullet-side rigid body would break Sync/Worker pose projection parity.

**Important scope distinction:** the joint rotation convention is *not* settled by these comparisons (Saba uses `setEulerZYX()` for joints). Investigate joint order separately; do not change it in this experiment.

## Expected outcome

**Try YXZ Euler composition for rigid-body offset rotations only**, in PMD and PMX, consistently in synchronous and Worker-backed physics. Use the already right-handed Euler values received from `mmd-parser`; do not change parser-side handedness conversion. Ensure `Rigidbody._init()`, native Bullet transforms, Worker-side stored offsets, and body-to-bone projection use the same convention.

Preserve joint-frame rotations at their currently implemented **XYZ** order. Since `setBasisFromArray3()` is shared by rigid-body and joint construction, do **not** simply switch its default behavior globally. Prefer an explicit order argument or separate named helper, avoiding changes to the joint path. The production behavior change should be limited to **rigid-body offset Euler composition**.

Treat this as an isolated MMD-compatibility experiment. Neither parameter tuning nor any other physics feature should be changed to mask the result.

### Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Change the rigid-body offset Euler composition from XYZ to **YXZ**, with an explicitly selected order at the relevant native transform creation call site. Keep all *joint* rotation frames as XYZ and document why this change is scoped only to rigid bodies.
- [ ] Apply the identical YXZ convention to Worker-side `WorkerPhysicsAdapter.offsets`, including body-pose initialization/reset, deferred inputs, and projection computations. The Worker runtime already uses the shared `MMDPhysics` code for its native rigid bodies. Do not duplicate incompatible conventions.
- [ ] Add deterministic independent **matrix/quaternion** reference tests (not just checking a property/string), comparing the resulting right-handed `Ry * Rx * Rz` rigid-body transform against a reference derived from the original PMD/PMX Euler angles and handedness reflection `diag(1,1,-1)`. Include nonzero multi-axis rotations (which distinguish XYZ from YXZ), single-axis rotations, identity, and reasonable angle edge cases. Verify both PMD and PMX parser→loader→physics paths and rigid-body offsets relative to bone transforms.
- [ ] Explicitly assert joint-frame transforms remain as before for a **multi-axis joint rotation**, not just axis-aligned/zero-angle fixtures. Do not change joint limits, springs, or STOP_ERP.
- [ ] Verify real Ammo initial body transforms, bone projection (types 0/1/2 as applicable), reset/warmup, and constrained poses using mixed-axis rigid bodies. Cover standalone Sync, shared Sync and Worker-owned paths (both browser transports where supported). Ensure the same selected rigid-body rotation maps back consistently from Bullet to bones, with numerical tolerance.
- [ ] Report which fixtures differ from the old XYZ behavior and whether the *raw rigid-body transforms* match the independent reference. Do not infer that visually correct MMD motion, greater stability, or violent-oscillation resolution is established by automated tests.
- [ ] Preserve the recently merged default timestep `unitStep = 1/60`, `maxStepNum = 10`, positive-delta accumulation, Worker scheduling/coalescing, gravity, additional damping, linked-body collision policy, Type-2 body authority, IK/grants, joint-frame rotation, joint limits, `STOP_ERP = 0.475`, renderer/materials and example lighting. No public A/B toggle. Keep this isolated from a future joint-order investigation.
- [ ] Run and report `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:examples`, applicable *local built-example* runtime checks, and `git diff --check`; clearly identify any unavailable/skipped tests.
- [ ] **Do not treat merged GitHub Pages publication or maintainer subjective visual validation as pre-merge PR approval/merge blockers.**

### Required post-merge verification

**PENDING until merge:** Check the merge-triggered [Deploy browser examples](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/actions/workflows/examples-pages.yml) workflow, using its **latest run attempt**, and record its URL, final outcome, deployed merge SHA/date and public site content verification. Verify the *public* PMD, Worker Physics and Gene Light PMX examples load without asset/runtime errors, recording evidence. Do not mark public checks as passed until actually verified; distinguish a successful Pages content-hash check from actual in-browser rendering/physics checks. If an HTTP 503 or timeout is transient, check retry attempts/results instead of asserting success from an earlier attempt.

**Optional post-merge maintainer evaluation, not a merge blocker:** Observe real PMD/PMX model visuals and physical motion, including possible effects on hair/skirt joints. Decide whether to retain or revert the new rigid-body convention. This is subjective follow-up, not proof provided by CI.

## Context

- Latest baseline at issue authoring: `main` at `1b308313ab088572f46856c8761504fa863dfba1`, with completed [#75 / PR #76](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/pull/76) and [#74 / PR #77](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/pull/77) timestep/substep experiments.
- [Three.js Euler default `XYZ`](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/src/math/Euler.js).
- [Saba rigid-body and joint conventions](https://github.com/benikabocha/saba/blob/master/src/Saba/Model/MMD/MMDPhysics.cpp); [babylon-mmd native Bullet backend](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/mmdBulletPhysics.ts).
- A future **separate** investigation should validate the joint Euler convention against MMD/Bullet; Saba and babylon-mmd do not provide an unambiguous basis to change it together with rigid bodies.
